sections.skill: Split a large task into stages you can check

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: What is the first stage in the passage's business-plan example?

choices.text: Ask for an outline and check it
Ask for the whole plan at once
Ask for a cover image
Ask for the final formatting first

questions.correct_answer: Ask for an outline and check it
questions.intro: Big jobs go better in STAGES. Instead of "write my whole business plan," ask first for an outline, check it, then draft one section at a time, checking each before moving on. Stages help because each step is small enough to review, mistakes are caught early instead of spreading through everything, and you stay in control of decisions. A good stage has a clear output you can check, such as a list of questions, an outline, a draft section, or a table of facts. Later stages can build on the approved earlier ones.
questions.feedback: An outline is a small, checkable first stage.

sections.skill: Compare stages with building a house

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: What is inspected first?

choices.text: The paint
The furniture
The foundation
The wiring

questions.correct_answer: The foundation
questions.intro: Builders do not put up a whole house in one step. First the FOUNDATION is poured and inspected. Then the FRAME goes up and is inspected. Then walls, wiring and paint. If the foundation is crooked, it is far cheaper to fix it before the frame is built on top. Each stage produces something an inspector can check. Breaking an AI task into stages works the same way: check the outline (the foundation) before building drafts on top of it.

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: A user approved an outline without reading it. It had a wrong date, and every section repeated it. What went wrong?

choices.text: Staging always causes wrong dates
The check between stages was skipped
Dates cannot be checked
The sections should have been written first

questions.correct_answer: The check between stages was skipped
questions.intro: Stages only help if you actually check between them. If an outline contains a wrong assumption and you approve it without reading, every later section inherits the mistake. Stages also need carrying forward: in a new conversation, the tool may not have the earlier approved parts, so paste them in. Not every task needs stages; a quick email does not. Use stages when a task is long, when early choices shape everything after, or when facts must be verified before writing.
